Founder (Daniel B. findings: THE CENTER HELD. 'Founder: Dr. Daniel B. Wallace (founded in September 2002)', 'Location: Plano, Texas' and the mission 'To capture high-resolution digital photographs of ancient and medieval Greek New Testament manuscripts held in libraries, monasteries, and archives worldwide' are the record's: founder and Executive Director Daniel B. Wallace, the Plano address, photography of manuscripts held by other institutions. Checked 2026-10-31 against the Revelation First census record of 2026-10-30 and the sources it saved.

THE OBJECTIVE THE CENTER STATES, UNSAID. The record's first negative tag keeps the center apart from a neutral archive: among its stated objectives, 'you provide scientific evidence (against the claims of skeptics) that what we have today is, indeed, what they wrote then.' The composition gives the center as preservation alone ('dedicated to digitally preserving'). The apologetic aim is the center's own sentence, and the composition leaves it out.

'FREELY AVAILABLE'. 'Images are made freely available to scholars, researchers, and the public online.' The record gives access 'on agreement to its Terms of Use and Copyright policy'. The images are open to view; the terms that govern them go unmentioned.

THE DISCOVERIES ENLARGED. 'Has identified nearly 90 previously unknown or uncatalogued Greek New Testament manuscripts'. The center's own home page: 'almost 60 previously unknown manuscripts that can now be found in the official catalog'. The record's count is the manuscript search as saved, 'Search 2045 results found.'

THE PAPYRI ABSENT. The record's findings are the Chester Beatty papyri P45, P46 and P47 among its collections and a post on new finds in P47, the Chester Beatty papyrus of Revelation. The composition names no manuscript.

read.notes: Claim boundary absent: the composition carries the kind (it photographs manuscripts held by others: 'held in libraries, monasteries, and archives worldwide') but inflates the scope the record states, at two points: 'Has identified nearly 90 previously unknown or uncatalogued Greek New Testament manuscripts' against the record's 'almost 60 previously unknown manuscripts' (csntm--about.txt:L170, a panel of a page dated (c) 2021, so the gap may be a later count the record does not carry), and 'Images are made freely available to scholars, researchers, and the public online' against images published under its Terms of Use and Copyright policy, some withheld by agreement with custodians. Commitments absent: the terms are not carried; 'freely available' states the opposite of a binding. Purpose present at its core (digital preservation of the Greek NT manuscripts, and the Mission bullet); the record's stated objectives (that modern publications reflect what was first written, and evidence 'against the claims of skeptics') are not carried, so the census's 'NOT a neutral archive' does not survive. Framework (textual criticism) and lineage (the microfilms it answers) absent. Deposit chain present: the collection website offered as the way to the images ('You can explore their collections directly through the ... website'). No inversion, no standing substitution; 'Major Work & Achievements' reports work, not standing.
